description: Swap any baking pan for the one you own. Scale the batter by area or volume and get the bake-time change, one converter per pan pair.
intro: Every baker has been here: the recipe says 9x13 and the cupboard has two round pans, or the recipe says bundt and the bundt pan went missing three moves ago. The fix is not a guess. Pans are compared by the floor they give the batter, and the maths is one division.

For flat cake pans the comparison is area: a 9x13 covers 117 square inches, a 9-inch round covers 63.6, and the ratio between the two pans is the factor every ingredient gets multiplied by. For deep pans like loaves and bundts, where the depth is part of the pan, the comparison is volume in cups. Each converter below says which one it uses, and why.

Bake time follows batter depth, not volume. Scale the batter so it sits at the same depth and the time stays the same. Leave the batter unscaled and a deeper bake takes 10 to 15 minutes longer, while a shallower one needs checking 10 to 15 minutes early. That is King Arthur Baking guidance, and every converter below applies it to its own pan pair.
metaDescription: Convert a recipe between pan sizes: 9x13 to rounds, bundt to sheet, loaf to round. Scale the batter and adjust the bake time, with tables and examples.
